metadata.title: Mutual Influence AI: Trust-Based Cooperation Mechanisms for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
metadata.venue: Advances in Electrical and Electronic Engineering
metadata.abstract_summary: Proposes trust-modulated cooperation among planner, researcher and critic LLM agents and evaluates it with convergence and agreement metrics such as rounds-to-approval; the approval-rate differences it reports were not statistically significant.

sections.heading: Claims
sections.text:
What the paper proposes or defines, as extracted (section, page):
- **Prompt and temperature modulation λ(µ), T(µ)** (category B) - Run-time schema mapping trust µ to a prompt-visible mixture hint and a sampling-temperature schedule for each LLM call. (section 3. Mutual Influence: Mathematical Formulation, p. 4)
  > used as a textual hint in the LLM prompt.
- **Two-round role orchestration protocol** (category B) - Schema for running planner, researcher, critic agents: one uninfluenced baseline round, feedback wiring, then one influence-modulated round with structured JSON outputs. (section 4. Experimental Plan and Metrics, p. 5)
  > Each run consists of two rounds: Round 1 (baseline) without influence modulation and Round 2 (influence) with µ–driven prompting and temperature scaling.
- **Cross-role agreement and intra-role stability** (category A) - Jaccard-based metrics for semantic overlap between roles and for each role's consistency across rounds. (section 3.1. Derived Evaluation Metrics, p. 4)
  > To quantify the semantic overlap between the two roles, we use the Jaccard index
- **Revision depth Drev** (category A) - Set-difference metric measuring how much content changes between successive draft rounds of the agent team. (section 3.1. Derived Evaluation Metrics, p. 4)
  > Larger Drev values correspond to deeper structural edits or significant content additions.
- **Rounds-to-Approval r*** (category A) - Convergence-speed metric counting dialogue rounds until the critic agent outputs APPROVE. (section 5.2. Discussion, p. 9)
  > the Rounds-to-Approval metric counts the number of conversational rounds until the critic outputs APPROVE, which we denote as r*

concepts.name: Prompt and temperature modulation λ(µ), T(µ)

sections.heading: Method
sections.text:
- **Prompt and temperature modulation λ(µ), T(µ)**: λi(t) = σ(k(µi(t) −τ)) = 1/(1 + e^{−k(µi(t)−τ)}); Ti(t) = T0/(1 + αµi(t)); prompti(t) = [µi(t), λi(t), Ti(t)] ∥user task.
- **Two-round role orchestration protocol**: Three MutualInfluenceAssistant roles; Round 1 uninfluenced; receive_feedback calls apply EMA trust; Round 2 prefixes (µ, λ, T). Each agent emits one JSON object per prompt with "features"; critic emits "decision" ∈{APPROVE, REVISE}.
- **Cross-role agreement and intra-role stability**: Across(t) = J(PF(t), RF(t)) = |PF(t) ∩ RF(t)| / |PF(t) ∪ RF(t)|; Splanner = J(PF(1), PF(2)), Sresearcher = J(RF(1), RF(2)).
- **Revision depth Drev**: Drev = |(PF(2) ∪ RF(2)) \ (PF(1) ∪ RF(1))|. Alternative form: RevisionDepth(t) = |N(t)| + δ(t), N(t) new points, δ(t) critic-feedback incorporation.
- **Rounds-to-Approval r***: r* counts conversational rounds until the critic outputs APPROVE; lower r* means faster convergence. Computed automatically from AutoGen conversation logs.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Evidence the authors report:
  - Prompt and temperature modulation λ(µ), T(µ): Ablation over (τ,k) on 167 runs: mean agreement peaks ≈0.58 at τ≈0.4, k≈3; stable for τ∈[0.45,0.55], k∈[4,6].
  - Two-round role orchestration protocol: 167 successful gpt-4o runs over β,k,τ,α sweep; 1,822 requests, 619,960 input tokens, $2.05 total cost.
  - Cross-role agreement and intra-role stability: Agreement rose 0.19→0.50 overall and 0.18→0.47 adversarial; Wilcoxon W=276 and W=138, both p<0.001, large Cliff's δ.
  - Revision depth Drev: Median revision depth ≈1.0 across 167 simulation runs, indicating shallow edits after influence-enabled round.
  - Rounds-to-Approval r*: Critic approval 35.8%→39.5% normal, 33.7%→26.7% adversarial; McNemar χ²=0.08, p=0.78 and χ²=0.54, p=0.46.
- Limitations the authors state:
  - Prompt and temperature modulation λ(µ), T(µ): If λ becomes too large, agents may converge prematurely to erroneous consensus; β, k, τ, α need careful per-application tuning.
  - Two-round role orchestration protocol: Costs scale approximately linearly with the number of agents and rounds; some grid combinations lost to timeouts and post-hoc filtering.
  - Rounds-to-Approval r*: Approval-rate differences were not statistically significant in either regime.
- Limitations they do not state: not assessed. Results are the authors' own, from their simulations, benchmarks or surveys; none evaluates delegation to cheaper models on software work.
